name: Durvalumab + Tremelimumab (STRIDE)
cyclesNote: STRIDE schedule: a single priming dose of tremelimumab 300 mg IV is given once with the first durvalumab dose (cycle 1, day 1 only); durvalumab 1500 mg IV then continues every 4 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Useful first-line when the anti-VEGF component of atezolizumab + bevacizumab is contraindicated.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event monitoring across organ systems; dual checkpoint blockade carries higher immune-toxicity risk than single agent.
Baseline and periodic thyroid, hepatic, adrenal, and glucose assessment; counsel prompt symptom reporting.
monitoring: symptom review for colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, dermatitis, endocrinopathy

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold therapy and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; permanently discontinue for severe or recurrent grade 3-4 events. Clinical review before rechallenge.

drugs.name: Tremelimumab
drugs.notes: Tremelimumab 300 mg IV as a SINGLE priming dose given once on cycle 1 day 1 only (not repeated in later cycles). Anti-CTLA-4 priming dose of the STRIDE regimen. Authored from standard practice (NCCN Hepatocellular Carcinoma; HIMALAYA / STRIDE supporting evidence).

drugs.name: Durvalumab
drugs.notes: Durvalumab 1500 mg IV flat on day 1 every 4 weeks, starting with the single tremelimumab priming dose and continuing as maintenance until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Authored from standard practice (NCCN Hepatocellular Carcinoma; HIMALAYA / STRIDE supporting evidence).
